subject: general
question: Which of the following is the primary reason why copper is widely used as a conductor in electrical wiring?

options.text: Copper has low resistance and high conductivity.
Copper has high resistance to electricity.
Copper has a low melting point.

solution:
The correct answer is __Copper has low resistance and high conductivity.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Copper__ is widely used as a conductor in electrical wiring due to its excellent properties.
 
• Copper has low resistance, which minimizes energy loss during transmission.
 
• The high conductivity of copper allows efficient current flow.
 
• It is durable and can withstand environmental factors such as humidity and temperature variations.
 
• Copper’s ductility makes it easy to draw into wires of various thicknesses.
 
• These characteristics make copper a preferred choice for electrical applications worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Aluminum:**

 
 
• Aluminum is also used in electrical wiring, especially for high-voltage transmission lines.
 
• Although it is less conductive than copper, it is much lighter and less expensive.
 
 
 
• **Silver: **
 
 
• Silver has the highest electrical conductivity of any metal.
 
• However, it is expensive and is rarely used in standard electrical wiring.
 
 
 
• **Gold:**
 
 
• Gold is used in small quantities for high-precision electronic components due to its resistance to corrosion.
 
• Its cost makes it impractical for regular electrical wiring.
